conventions: Formatter is Prettier with the @backstage/cli config: 2 spaces, single quotes, trailing commas, arrow parens avoided, 80 columns. Every file is formatted by the prettier check's write form, so do not fight it.
Every new .ts, .tsx and .js source file starts with the Apache 2.0 header reading `Copyright 2026 The Backstage Authors`. Existing files keep their year. Docs, YAML and changesets carry no header.
Named exports only; no default exports except the migration's `exports.up` and `exports.down`. Public API carries a TSDoc release tag; internals use `@internal` or none, matching the file.

Backend source uses `node:` prefixes for built-ins and throws `@backstage/errors` types for the shared middleware to serialize. Frontend code uses function components, `useApi`, and `react-use/esm/*` import paths.
User-visible frontend text goes through the package's translation ref with `useTranslationRef` from `@backstage/core-plugin-api/alpha`.
Entity refs in the database are lowercase `kind:namespace/name`; produce them with `stringifyEntityRef`, never by hand.
All SQL goes through Knex and must work on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite: no dialect-specific SQL, no boolean bindings, and timestamps come from `tx.fn.now()`.

Tests are Jest `describe`/`it`, in fewer thorough cases with several assertions. React tests use `screen` with `findBy*` over `waitFor` and add no test IDs. Database tests use `TestDatabases.create()` and `describe.each(databases.eachSupportedId())`.

Never hand-edit `src/schema/openapi/generated/**` or `report*.api.md`; tooling units write them. Never touch `package.json`, `yarn.lock`, `plugins/catalog-backend/report.sql.md`, or `queries.md` and `baseline.md`, and keep each file's Zod import as it is.

Docs follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: U.S. English, second person, friendly but direct, code style for paths, annotations and refs, bold for UI elements, italics for a new term on first use.

Changesets are hand-written `.changeset/*.md` files with front matter naming package and bump, written for adopters in plain language, naming no internal symbol. Public API names such as `getEntityByFormerRef` are allowed.

decisions.choice: `backstage.io/former-entity-refs`, exported from `@backstage/catalog-model` as `ANNOTATION_FORMER_ENTITY_REFS`. The value is comma-separated full refs; each piece is trimmed, empty pieces are skipped, and pieces are lowercased before validation and deduplicated.
rejected: a new `metadata` field, which needs envelope schema changes
decisions.reason: Annotations are the catalog's existing extension point and FR-1 asks for one.

decisions.choice: Route `GET /entities/by-former-name/{kind}/{namespace}/{name}` with operationId `GetEntityByFormerName`; client method `getEntityByFormerRef(entityRef, options)` on `CatalogApi` and `CatalogService`; internal method `EntitiesCatalog.entityByFormerRef(request)`.
decisions.reason: Mirrors `by-name`, `getEntityByRef` and `entitiesBatch`, so every layer reads as a sibling of the exact lookup.

decisions.choice: Table `former_entity_refs`: `former_entity_ref` string not null, `claimant_entity_id` string not null with FK to `refresh_state.entity_id` ON DELETE CASCADE, `claimant_entity_ref` string not null, `claimed_at` dateTime not null, `rejected_at` dateTime nullable. Primary key (`former_entity_ref`, `claimant_entity_id`); index `former_entity_refs_claimant_entity_id_idx` on `claimant_entity_id`.
rejected: a boolean `rejected` column, because booleans bind and read differently per engine
keying on `claimant_entity_ref` with no FK, because every deletion path would then need its own cleanup
decisions.reason: The FK makes every existing deletion path remove claims with no code change, and `whereNull('rejected_at')` is portable.

decisions.topic: What counts as a live holder
decisions.choice: A ref is held when `refresh_state` has a row with that `entity_ref`, in both claim recording and lookup. A missing location key (null, undefined or empty) never matches, including missing against missing.
rejected: `final_entities`, which misses an entity that exists but is not stitched yet
decisions.reason: `refresh_state` has a unique index on `entity_ref` and reflects what the catalog holds now; C-6 requires failing closed.

decisions.choice: A rejection is decided only when a row is first inserted: if a holder exists and its location key does not match the claimant's, `rejected_at` is set and is never cleared; the row only goes away when the claimant stops declaring the ref. Per ref, the winner is the first row with `rejected_at` null ordered by `claimed_at` then `claimant_entity_ref`. For a claimant's report: own row rejected gives `rejected`; else not the winner gives `lost`; else `active`. Whether a holder exists never adds an error, so held claims stay silent (FR-8) and the lookup alone decides if a claim is in effect.
decisions.reason: Outcomes derive from rows, so takeover and reactivation need no re-ingestion, and the winner is stable across reprocessing (D2, D3).

decisions.choice: In `DefaultCatalogProcessingEngine`, after `orchestrator.process` and only when `result.ok`, before the result hash is built, in its own `retryOnDeadlock` transaction. Claim errors join `result.errors` in a local `errors` list used for the event, `errorsString` and so the hash; `result.ok` is untouched. The engine calls the operation directly with `tx as Knex.Transaction`, the way it calls `markForStitching`, so `ProcessingDatabase` gains no method.
rejected: a catalog processor, because any emitted error sets `ok: false` and drops the entity (C-1)
the orchestrator, which has no database access
decisions.reason: This is the only point that keeps ingestion unblocked (FR-6) and still changes the hash when only a claim's outcome changed (FR-7).

decisions.topic: No query for entities that never declare
decisions.choice: The sync runs only when the annotation is present or the refresh state cache JSON holds the marker `formerEntityRefClaims: true`. The engine sets that marker after a sync that left at least one valid declared ref, drops it after a sync that left none, and keeps it through the failed-processing branch that otherwise resets the state to `{}`.
rejected: a delete in `updateProcessedEntity`, which adds a query for every changed entity (NFR-2)
a new `refresh_state` column, which changes the select of `getProcessableEntities` (FR-24)
decisions.reason: An entity that drops the annotation still needs its claims removed, and only this keeps never-declaring entities free of any query.

decisions.choice: All are `InputError`, in annotation order, naming only the declared value. Invalid: `Ignored former entity ref '<value>' in annotation backstage.io/former-entity-refs: <reason>`, where reason is one of `it is not a full entity ref on the form kind:namespace/name`, `it has a different kind from this entity`, `it is this entity's own ref`. Rejected: `Former entity ref '<ref>' was rejected because another source held that ref when it was first claimed. To clear this, remove the value from annotation backstage.io/former-entity-refs, then add it back once the old entity is gone`. Lost: `Former entity ref '<ref>' is not in effect because another entity claimed it first`.
decisions.reason: Stable text keeps the result hash stable, and FR-4 and the PII inventory fix what each message may say.

decisions.choice: Every miss is `NotFoundError` with the message `No entity found with former ref '<lowercase requested ref>'`, thrown by `writeSingleEntityResponse`. A hit is 200 with the entity JSON. No other field is added.
decisions.reason: FR-12 requires one response for all misses; the message echoes only what the caller sent.

decisions.topic: Carrying the former ref to the notice
decisions.choice: Frontend redirects call `navigate(target, { replace: true, state: { formerEntityRef } })`, where `formerEntityRef` is the lowercase ref of the old URL. Notices read `useLocation().state?.formerEntityRef` and show only a string value.
rejected: a query parameter, which alters the kept query and lets any link fake a notice (C-7)
decisions.reason: Location state cannot be set by a crafted link, which gives NFR-6.

decisions.choice: The two MUI layouts and the TechDocs reader render a dismissible MUI `Snackbar` holding an `Alert severity="info"`, top center. `EntityLayoutBui` renders a BUI `Alert status="info"` in flow, above the tab content. Text keys are `entityPage.renamedNotice` in `catalogTranslationRef` and `reader.renamedNotice` in `techdocsTranslationRef`, both `This entity was renamed from {{formerEntityRef}}.`.
rejected: an in-flow alert in `Page`, whose grid places `pageContent` children on top of each other
`alertApi`, which depends on the app mounting `AlertDisplay`
decisions.reason: A Snackbar stays out of the `Page` grid; the BUI layout is plain flow and can hold the alert inline.

decisions.choice: `useFormerEntityRef` lives in `plugins/catalog/src/components/EntityLayout/EntityRenamedNotice.tsx`, and no layout imports `useEntityFromUrl`.
decisions.reason: `plugin.lazy.test.tsx` fails if the alpha plugin loads `useEntityFromUrl` eagerly, and the legacy layout is loaded eagerly.

decisions.choice: `useEntityFromUrl` gets its route from a private `useOptionalEntityRoute()` that wraps `useRouteRef` from `@backstage/core-plugin-api` in try/catch and returns undefined on any throw. This follows `useRouteResolutionApi` in `packages/core-plugin-api/src/routing/useRouteRef.tsx` lines 46-52, and `packages/core-plugin-api/src/extensions/extensions.tsx` lines 88-105 already wraps `useRouteRef` itself in a try/catch. With no route, or when the route function throws, the former lookup ends as `{}` and the existing not-found page renders. `EntityHeaderBui` moves its owner links into a child rendered only for an entity with owners, as its `HierarchyLinks` does, so the not-found page never calls `useEntityRefLink`.
rejected: `useRouteRef` unguarded, which throws `No path for` on an unbound ref in both systems: `useRouteRef.tsx` line 146 in the old system and line 131 in the new one

`useRouteRef` from `@backstage/frontend-plugin-api`, which returns undefined in the new system, but whose `useApi` at line 56 throws in the old system before its remaining hooks run, so a try/catch around it changes the hook count
a try/catch around `useEntityRefLink`, which throws at line 85 before its `useCallback` at line 87, so the hook count changes whenever the throw depends on the pathname
changing `useEntityRefLink` or `useRouteRef` to return undefined, because both files are outside the allowlist and both are public contracts
reading `routeResolutionApiRef` and the routing context directly, which copies `useRouteRef` and still needs a try/catch
decisions.reason: Inside a Router, core `useRouteRef` runs the same hooks on every render, throw or not: its `useLocation` throws only outside a Router, where the earlier `useNavigate` has already thrown uncaught; `useApi` throws inside the caught `useRouteResolutionApi`; its only throw during a hook is in the callback of its last `useMemo`, whose slot React allocates before running the callback (`mountMemo` and `updateMemo` in react-dom 18.3.1); and the other throws come after its last hook. So this try/catch cannot change the hook order.

decisions.choice: `TechDocsReaderPage` is standalone when `props.entityRef` is undefined. It passes `{ followFormerRef: true }` to `useExternalRedirect` and renders the notice only then. The redirect URL is computed inside the async lookup, from `viewTechdocLink(getCompoundEntityRef(entity))`, not `buildTechDocsURL`.
rejected: `buildTechDocsURL`, which adds the external path and would break keeping the sub-path
decisions.reason: Embedded docs are covered by the entity-page redirect (FR-21), and an entity page that already shows the notice must not show a second one.

decisions.choice: A tooling unit runs `backstage-repo-tools api-reports` directly with the flags of `build:api-reports` less `--sql-reports`, limited by positional paths to the seven affected packages.
rejected: `yarn build:api-reports`, which always passes `--sql-reports` and would write `report.sql.md` (FR-26)
writing that file and restoring it afterwards, which D4 forbids
decisions.reason: Paths also keep the step inside the write contract if an unrelated package's report has drifted.

decisions.choice: `minor` for `@backstage/catalog-model`, `@backstage/catalog-client`, `@backstage/plugin-catalog-node`, `@backstage/plugin-catalog-react`, `@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend`, `@backstage/plugin-catalog` and `@backstage/plugin-techdocs`. `@backstage/plugin-techdocs-react` changes nothing and gets none.
decisions.reason: All are at 1.0.0 or above and gain non-breaking features or API, and D1 fixes `minor` for the client and node packages.
